 Interested in ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better. 
 Strong quarterly results: Q3 revenue rose 21% to CNY 14.4 billion and operating profit climbed 23.8% to CNY 2.98 billion. Parcel volume grew 7%, lifting ZTO's market share to 20.1% even as industry growth slowed. 
 Guidance maintained amid a slower market: ZTO kept its 2026 parcel-volume forecast of 40.83 billion to 42.37 billion, or 6% to 10% growth. Management expects industry growth to remain slower but aims to outperform through better service and higher-quality market share. 
 Cost control and buybacks: Transportation and sorting costs per parcel fell 2.8%, helping offset fuel-cost pressure. ZTO had repurchased about $1.05 billion of shares year to date under its $1.4 billion program and plans to complete the remaining purchases as conditions permit. 
 3 must-own China stocks for the Year of the Dragon 
 ZTO Express (Cayman) (NYSE:ZTO) reported higher third-quarter revenue and operating profit as parcel volumes grew faster than the broader industry, and the delivery company maintained its full-year volume guidance despite slowing sector growth. 
 Revenue rose 21% year over year to CNY 14.4 billion in the third quarter of 2026, while operating profit increased 23.8% to CNY 2.98 billion. Parcel volume reached 10.24 billion, up 7%, lifting market share by 0.7 percentage points to 20.1%, Chairman and CEO Meisong Lai said in remarks translated by Director of Capital Markets Sophie Li.

 Industry parcel volume growth slowed to 2.9% as anti-involution policies, which management said are intended in part to discourage below-cost competition, continued to take effect. Lai said the competitive landscape was gradually normalizing, although prices fluctuated in some regions. 
 Growth and Profitability 
 Adjusted net income increased 2.6% to CNY 2.57 billion. CFO Huiping Yan said adjusted net income growth was 20.7% after excluding a CNY 376 million tax refund received in the third quarter of the prior year. The comparable refund was received in the second quarter this year.

 Retail parcel volume rose 57% year over year. Lai said through a translator that improvements in service and the last-mile network had supported retail and reverse-logistics business, while giving couriers access to market prices helped encourage pickups and improve their earnings. 
 Story Continues Management also acknowledged pressure on reverse-logistics profitability. Lai said platform auctions had weighed on prices, although higher volume and tighter cost controls partly offset the effect. He expects retail and reverse-logistics volumes to continue growing. 
 → Intuitive Machines' Business Is Taking Off—Will Its Stock Follow? 
 Core express delivery average selling price rose CNY 0.16, or 13.7%, as the product mix shifted toward higher-value key account volume, including fast-growing reverse logistics, Yan said. Gross profit increased 19.5% to CNY 3.5 billion, although gross margin narrowed 0.3 percentage points to 24.6%. Operating margin expanded 0.4 percentage points to 20.7%. 
 Costs and Industry Outlook 
 Combined transportation and sorting costs per parcel fell CNY 0.02, or 2.8%, despite higher oil prices. Unit line-haul transportation costs declined 5.8% to CNY 0.32, while sorting costs remained flat at CNY 0.25. 
 Lai said through a translator that higher fuel prices added about CNY 0.01 per parcel to transportation costs in the third quarter. ZTO expects a similar or slightly greater impact in the fourth quarter. The company is expanding its natural gas truck fleet, testing electric vehicles on selected routes and using its own fuel stations to seek better diesel supplies. 
 Management attributed transportation savings partly to a dispatch system that adjusts schedules, routes and capacity, as well as fleet-management measures. At sorting centers, automation and labor productivity improvements offset higher depreciation and amortization associated with newly commissioned facilities, Lai said. 
 Looking ahead, Lai said slower volume growth is likely to become the industry norm, but ZTO expects to continue growing faster than the sector by improving service and pursuing higher-quality market share. He said industry pricing had recovered meaningfully since anti-involution measures began, and that prices in key markets including Yiwu and Hebei had recovered entering peak season. 
 Management also expects the gradual expansion of social insurance and occupational injury coverage to put some near-term pressure on per-parcel costs across the industry. Lai said stronger coverage could support network stability and last-mile service quality over time. 
 Guidance and Shareholder Returns 
 ZTO maintained its 2026 parcel volume forecast of 40.83 billion to 42.37 billion parcels, representing year-over-year growth of 6% to 10%. Yan said the outlook reflects management's preliminary view and remains subject to change. The company expects full-year capital expenditure of about CNY 6 billion, after spending CNY 1.3 billion in the third quarter. 
 Operating cash flow rose 15.9% to CNY 3.7 billion, and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased 14.3% to CNY 4.1 billion. 
 In response to an analyst's question about shareholder returns, Lai said through a translator that ZTO had repurchased approximately $1.05 billion of shares year to date under a $1.4 billion program funded by the net proceeds of a convertible bond offering. The company intends to complete the remaining purchases as market conditions permit. 
 Management expects this year's repurchase spending to exceed 100% of last year's net profit and does not plan to pay an additional dividend this year. Lai said the company's standing return program calls for annual shareholder returns of at least 50% of the previous year's net profit, taking free cash and profit levels into consideration. 
 About ZTO Express (Cayman) (NYSE:ZTO) 
 ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc. is a China-based express delivery and logistics company. It provides parcel collection, sorting, transportation and delivery services, serving e-commerce businesses, merchants and individual customers. The company operates a network of service outlets, transportation partners and sorting hubs across China. Its services also include freight forwarding, warehousing and cross-border logistics through its international business. Founded in 2002, ZTO is headquartered in Shanghai.
